name: Larry Page

summary.text: Larry Page co-founded Google with Sergey Brin and was chief executive of Google and then of its parent Alphabet until December 3, 2019, when he and Brin stepped down and Sundar Pichai became Alphabet CEO; both founders stayed on the board as major shareholders. As Google CEO in September 2013 he announced Calico, a company focused on aging and associated diseases led by Genentech chairman Arthur Levinson, and Google acquired DeepMind in 2014 during his tenure. Elon Musk has said that Page called him a 'specieist' during an argument about AI, and testified in April 2026 that the dispute drove him to found OpenAI.

facts.claim: On September 18, 2013 Google announced Calico, a new company focused on health and well-being and in particular aging and associated diseases. Arthur D. Levinson, chairman and former CEO of Genentech and chairman of Apple, became its CEO and a founding investor. Page said: 'Illness and aging affect all our families. With some longer term, moonshot thinking around healthcare and biotechnology, I believe we can improve millions of lives.'
facts.quote: Illness and aging affect all our families. With some longer term, moonshot thinking around healthcare and biotechnology, I believe we can improve millions of lives.

sources.title: Google announces Calico, a new company focused on health and well-being

facts.claim: Page told Time in 2013 that it could be 10 to 20 years before Calico's work bore fruit; Google did not disclose its funding, and Page indicated it would not be a major commitment.
facts.quote: In a Time interview, he suggested it could be 10 to 20 years before Calico's efforts bear fruit. Google did not disclose the funding, but Page indicated it won't be a major commitment.

facts.claim: On December 3, 2019 Page and Sergey Brin announced they were stepping down as CEO and president of Alphabet, with Google CEO Sundar Pichai also becoming Alphabet CEO. Both remained on the board as major shareholders, saying Alphabet and Google now operated effectively independently so it was time to simplify the management structure.
facts.quote: Sundar Pichai, the CEO of Google, will also be the CEO of Alphabet. Both Page and Brin, the major shareholders, will remain on the company board.

facts.claim: Elon Musk has said that, during an argument about AI, Page called him a 'specieist' for favouring humans over machine intelligence; Business Insider, citing The New York Times, placed the exchange at Musk's 2015 birthday party in Napa Valley, while Walter Isaacson's biography dates it to 2013. Musk has said Page wanted 'digital superintelligence, basically digital God' as soon as possible. In April 2026 Musk testified at his trial against OpenAI that the insult drove him to found OpenAI.
facts.quote: Musk testified that the insult drove him to found OpenAI

openQuestions: Reports that Page spoke at Singularity University's 2008 founding meeting came from an SU briefing hosted on a third-party site and were left out.
Accounts of the 'specieist' exchange rest on Musk's own telling, Isaacson's biography and Max Tegmark's Life 3.0; Page has not been found to have commented.
